newsitem.title: FRANCE: Remy-Cointreau first-half profit goes flat.
newsitem.headline: Remy-Cointreau first-half profit goes flat.

text.p: French cognac and champagne maker Remy-Cointreau reported an 81 percent drop in pre-tax profits for the first half of fiscal 1996-1997 Tuesday due to a fall in one-time gains related to a prior debt restructuring.
The company, best known for Remy Martin cognacs and Krug and Piper-Heidsieck champagnes, partly blamed the decline on a drop in cognac sales in Asia and Europe.
Remy said pretax income for the six months ending Sept. 30 fell to 41 million francs ($7.8 million) from 215 million francs ($40.8 million) in the year-ago period.

Its pretax loss before one-time charges shrank to 1 million francs ($190,000) from 39 million francs ($7.4 million), and Remy said it expected the improving trend to be helped by a "satisfying" level of activity seen at the start of the second half begun in October.
Sales rose 4 percent to 3.07 billion francs ($584 million) in the first half after a rebound in the second quarter from a weak first quarter.
Managing Director Marc Heriard Dubreuil said cognac sales in Japan were still falling, but a slide in cognac sales in China, where Remy is a market leader, halted at mid-year.

"Our (cognac) sales are more difficult in Europe, in Britain and France," he told a news conference. "The economic climate in Europe isn't conducive to spending for expensive drinks," he said, but added that sales were strong in the United States.
The company's biggest brands have resumed growth and Remy is focusing on developing its distribution network for other brands, most recently through an agreement to sell Seagram liquors in Barbados.
